can_do: I can say what was arranged and did not happen.
I can mark a plan that failed without blaming the wrong thing.

grammar.label: unrealised past plans — was to have, were to have, might have been
grammar.form: was / were + to have + past participle; might / could have been + -ing
grammar.meaning: says what was arranged or expected and then did not happen

explanation.en: 'The road was to have opened in May' — it was arranged, and it did not. Compare 'the road was to open in May', which only says what the plan was, without implying it failed. The extra 'have' carries the whole meaning. 'She might have been running the department by now' does the same for an expectation.
explanation.uz: 'The road was to have opened in May' — rejalashtirilgan edi va amalga oshmadi. 'was to open' esa faqat rejani bildiradi, muvaffaqiyatsizlikni emas. Butun ma'no qo'shimcha 'have' da.

grammar.positive_example: The inquiry was to have reported in March; its findings appeared two years later.
grammar.negative_example: The inquiry was to report in March; its findings appeared two years later.

l1_notes.uz: Bu nozik farq o'zbek va rus tillarida alohida shakl bilan berilmaydi; kontekstdan chiqadi, shuning uchun o'rganish qiyin.

grammar.label: modal harmony — stacking hedges without contradicting yourself
grammar.form: modal + adverb of the same strength (may possibly, must surely, could conceivably)
grammar.meaning: keeps the strength of a claim consistent across the sentence

explanation.en: A modal and its adverb should agree in strength. 'It may possibly be true' is harmonic. 'It must possibly be true' is not — 'must' is strong and 'possibly' is weak, and the sentence reads as confused rather than careful. At C1 the skill is to pick one level of confidence and hold it through modal, adverb and reporting verb alike.
explanation.uz: Modal va ravish kuchi bo'yicha mos kelishi kerak. 'It may possibly be true' — mos. 'It must possibly be true' — mos emas: 'must' kuchli, 'possibly' kuchsiz.

grammar.positive_example: The delay may well have been deliberate, though the file does not say so.
grammar.negative_example: The delay must possibly have been deliberate, though the file does not say so.

l1_notes.uz: Ko'p o'quvchilar ehtiyotkorlikni ko'proq hedging bilan ifodalashga harakat qiladi; natijada gap ma'nosini yo'qotadi.

story.title: The inquiry was to have reported

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Whatever happened to the inquiry into the road being closed in 2019?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It was to have reported in March.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: 'Was to have.' So it did not.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It did not. Two members resigned and nobody replaced them.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That extra 'have' is doing all the work. 'The inquiry was to report in March' would only tell me the plan.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I have used it three times on one page. Is that too many?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Three failures on one page is what you are describing. The form is not the problem.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Here I wrote 'the delay must possibly have been deliberate'.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That is two different strengths in one sentence. 'Must' is certain and 'possibly' is not.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The delay may well have been deliberate.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Better. And then either give me the evidence or take the sentence out.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then take it out. A hint you cannot support is worse than nothing, because a careful reader will spend an hour looking for what is not there.
